texts.facts: Page 1 of 39 Awar D The Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed on 14.10.2023 was registered as a Motor Accident Claim petition. The DAR revealed that a Road Traffic Accident took place on 16.07.2023 at about 05.38 AM at DBG Road Near Red Light, Rani Jhansi Round About, Pahar Ganj, Delhi wherein the petitioner, Mr. Vikash had sustained grievous injuries. The accident took place with a vehicle bearing registration No. Vikash vs Dhirender Singh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19691879/ 1 DL 1LAG 0502 driven by respondent no.1, Mr. Dheerender Singh; owned by respondent no. 2, Mr. Sohan Singh Rawat and insured with respondent no. 3, Go Digit General Insurance Co. Ltd. BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE: 2. The brief facts that have emerged from the DAR are that on 16.07.2023, the information of an accident was received at P.S. Pahar Ganj vide DD No. 032A by ASI Ravi Kumar. On receiving the said information, ASI Ravi Kumar along with Ct. Deepak, immediately went to the spot of the accident i.e. Rani Jhansi Road Gol Chakkar, where one vehicle bearing registration no. DL 1LAG 0502 make Supro Mini Truck (Chhota Hathi) was found turned over towards driver's side and blood was found blowing from the window at the driver's side. Neither the injured nor the PCR caller was found there. The public persons, who were present at the spot of the accident, informed him that the injured had been taken to LHMC Hospital. Then ASI Ravi called the Crime Team at the spot of the accident. The Crime Team inspected the spot of the accident and took photographs. ASI Ravi collected the exhibits from the spot of the accident and after leaving Ct. Deepak at the spot of the accident, he went to LHMC Hospital where the injured Vikash was found under treatment vide MLC No. 1283/2023 wherein the doctor had mentioned the alleged history to be "RTA at Jhandewalan Hours before" and the doctor had stated the injured to be not fit for statement. He could not find any eye witness of the accident despite his best efforts. On the basis of PCR call and the MLC of the injured, the offence under Section 279/337 IPC was found to have been committed and accordingly, ASI Ravi prepared a hand written complaint and sent Ct. Deepak to P.S. Paharganj who got the FIR No. 503/2023 registered. 3. During the course of the investigation, the IO took the blood samples and report of the Crime Team from the place of accident. He prepared the site plan of the spot of the accident and got the offending vehicle/accidental vehicle straightened with the help of crane and deposited the same in the Malkhana. Thereafter, the IO again went to LHMC Hospital where he was informed that the injured has been taken to Safdarjung Hospital by his relatives. Then the IO along with Ct. Deepak went to Safdarjung Hospital and recorded the statement of the injured Vikash who stated that he had been working as helper with the courier and cargo company in the name and style of Whiteline Airways, Jhandewalan, Pahar Ganj for the last 7-8 years and his work was of loading and unloading. He further stated that on the date of the accident i.e. 16.07.2023 at about 5.00 A.M., he was going to Lahori Gate for delivery of material of the company after loading the same in the vehicle bearing registration no. DL 1LAG 0502 which was being driven by respondent no.1, Dheerender Singh and when they reached at main DBG Road, the driver of the said vehicle started to drive at a very high speed in rash and negligent manner. The injured also stated that he even asked the driver not to drive fast but he did not stop rather said that "Tujhe nahi pata ki dheere chalenge to no entry ho jayegi". When they reached near Rani Jhansi Gol Chakkar, he turned the vehicle very dangerously and the vehicle toppled over and the injured fell towards driver's side and got injured. After some time, another boy from the company namely Jail Prakash came there and took the injured to the hospital in an auto. After recording of the statement of the injured, the IO returned to the police station and contacted the owner of the offending vehicle who stated himself to be out of station and ensured that he will join the investigation after he returns. On 17.07.2023, the IO made enquiry Vikash vs Dhirender Singh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19691879/ 2 from Mr. Rohit Rawat, son of the owner of the offending vehicle, and recorded his statement. On 19.07.2023, the IO got the mechanical inspection of the offending vehicle conducted. 4. During the further course of investigation, on 22.07.2024, the owner of the offending vehicle, Sh. Sohan Singh Rawat came to the police station. The IO served notice under Section 133 M.V. Act upon him who replied in writing that Sh. Dheerender Singh was driving the said vehicle at the time of the accident. The driver was arrested by the IO, however, as the offence was bailable, he was released on bail on furnishing of bail bonds. The IO also seized the driving license of respondent no. 1 as well as all the documents related to the offending vehicle. Thereafter, IO deposited the MLC of the injured in Safdarjung Hospital for final opinion as per which, the injury was found to be 'grievous' and therefore, section 338 of IPC was added. On completion of investigation, chargesheet under section 279/338 IPC was filed against the driver Dheerender Singh and DAR was filed before the court on 14.10.2023. 5. Respondent nos.1 & 2 had filed their written statement on 23.11.2023 and reply on behalf of respondent no. 2 was filed on 18.11.2023. ISSUES FRAMED 6. OPP. (iii) Relief. EVIDENCE 7. To prove his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1. Respondent no.1 examined himself as RW-1, respondent no. 2 examined himself as RW-2 and respondent no. 3 examined Sh. Paramvir Singh as R3W-1. 8. The Petitioner filed the Form XIV. Financial statement of the petitioner has been recorded. The petitioner/injured has not claimed any amount under this head. Compensation for disfiguration: 32. DISBURSEMENT 39. The Financial Statement of the petitioner/injured was recorded by this Court/Tribunal. As per the said statement, the monthly expenses of his family are approximately Rs. 22,000/- per month.
texts.arguments: Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287). In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion. 16. Furthermore, in view of filing of DAR containing the charge-sheet for the offences u/s 279/338 IPC and other relevant documents against the respondent no.1 and in terms of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, respondent no.1 Dheerender Singh (driver of the offending vehicle) is held to be negligent on the basis of preponderance of probability. Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases. In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under: "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result Vikash vs Dhirender Singh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19691879/ 7 of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467). 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads Vikash vs Dhirender Singh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19691879/ 8 (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. We may however note that in some cases, on appreciation of evidence and assessment, the Tribunal may find that percentage of loss of earning capacity as a result of the permanent disability, is approximately the same as the percentage of permanent disability in which case, of course, the Tribunal will adopt the said percentage for determination of compensation (see for example, the decisions of this court in Arvind Kumar Mishra vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. - 2010(10) SCALE 298 and Yadava Kumar v. D.M., National Insurance Co. Ltd. - 2010 (8) SCALE 567). 9. After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the Vikash vs Dhirender Singh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19691879/ 10 medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity. 10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps. The determination of damages on account of pain and suffering, loss of amenities and loss of expectation of life would depend upon the age of Vikash vs Dhirender Singh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19691879/ 11 victim, nature of injury(ies)/deprivation/disability suffered by victim and the effect thereof on life of the petitioner. An appropriate multiplier needs to be ascertained as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in matter of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC 2009 ACJ 1298 SC according to age of the injured/victim. The petitioner has claimed Rs.10,000/- under the head conveyance charges but there is no cogent evidence for the same. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 40,000/- under the head attendant charges but there is no cogent evidence for the same. The petitioner/injured has claimed Rs. 5,00,000/- under this head. The petitioner has not filed anything on record to prove his claim, however, taking into account the injuries suffered by him and also noticing the disability suffered by him, Rs. 50,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head. Compensation for loss of marriage prospects: 33. The petitioner/injured has claimed Rs. 10,00,000/- under this head. The petitioner has not filed anything on record to prove his claim, however, taking into account the injuries suffered by him and also noticing the disability suffered by him, Rs. 1,00,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head. Compensation for loss of earning, inconvenience, hardships, disappointment, frustration, mental stress, dejectment and unhappiness in future life etc.: 34. Vikash vs Dhirender Singh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19691879/ 14 Future loss of income: 35. The petitioner Sh. Vikash has claimed loss of earning considering functional disability of 50%. Ld. Counsel for the petitioner argued that the petitioner has suffered loss of income due to the disability albeit temporary and therefore, his loss must be compensated. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3 argued that the disability suffered by the petitioner is only 13% which is also temporary in nature and even as per the opinion of the doctor, it is likely to be improved. 36. The disability certificate shows that the petitioner/ injured has suffered 13% physical disability. The medical board has further concluded that the said disability is temporary in nature. It has been opined that the disability can improve. Further, there is nothing on record to show that the income of the petitioner/ injured has been affected due to the injuries suffered by him in the accident. In view of this, as the disability of the petitioner/ injured is temporary in nature and is likely to be improved, this Tribunal is not inclined to grant any compensation under the head future loss of income. Counsel for respondent no. 3 argued that the petitioner/injured was an unauthorised occupant and thus, he was not covered under the policy and thus, the liability cannot be fastened upon the insurance company. 46. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the petitioners argued that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle as the authorised representative of the goods that were being transported in the goods carriage and therefore, he was not an unauthorized passenger and the risk with respect to him is, thus, covered in the insurance policy. 47. From the above arguments of Ld. Counsels for the petitioner and respondent no.3, the first point that arises for consideration is whether the deceased was traveling in the offending vehicle as the authorised representative of the goods or not. 50. Further, Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 provides as follows: "147. Requirement of policies and limits of liability: (1) In order to comply with the requirements of this Chapter, a policy of insurance must be a policy which- (a) is issued by a person who is an authorised insurer; and (b) insures the person or classes of persons specified in the policy to the extent specified in sub-section (2) - (i) against any liability which may be incurred by him in respect of the death of or bodily injury to any person including owner of the goods or his authorised representative carried in the motor vehicle or damage to any property of a third party caused by or arising out of the use of the motor vehicle in a public place; (ii) against the death of or bodily injury to any passenger of a transport vehicle, except gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle, caused by or arising out of the use of the motor vehicle in a public place." 51. Thus, clause b(i) of sub section 1 of section 147 of the MV Act makes it a statutory obligation on the part of the insurance company to cover any bodily injury or death upon the owner of the goods Vikash vs Dhirender Singh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19691879/ 20 as well as the authorised representative of the owner of the goods.
